https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/cia-dir.text: Search Advertisement Advertise with NZME. Director of the CIA John Ratcliffehas made an unannounced trip to Russia. Photo / Getty Images CIA director John Ratcliffe arrived in Moscow on Tuesday, people familiar with the matter said, for a rare visit by a US spy agency chief as Russia slogs through its fifth year of war in Ukraine. US officials had not announced Ratcliffe’s trip but publicly available flight-tracking data captured the movement of a US government transport plane from Joint Base Andrews on the outskirts of Washington to the Russian capital. The CIA, the Pentagon and the US Air Force declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Those familiar with Ratcliffe’s trip to Russia spoke on the condition of anonymity. It was not immediately clear what the trip’s purpose was or whether any other senior US officials were part of the US delegation. Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow coincides with a fraught period in US-Russia relations. Russia and Ukraine have stepped up long-range strikes on each other’s territory with no end to the war in sight. Some analysts have warned that Russian President Vladimir Putin might escalate with military probes against Europe’s Baltic countries or other Nato members, which could precipitate a new crisis. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. The two superpowers are on opposite sides of the Iran conflict. Iran is Moscow’s most important ally in the Middle East, and Russia has provided Tehran targeting intelligence on the location of US military assets in the region. The US Treasury on Monday unveiled a sweeping campaign of sanctions and diplomatic pressure meant to asphyxiate Iran’s economy. The Kremlin was mum about the visit. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov initially said the Kremlin had no information about the US military aircraft that arrived at Moscow’s Vnukovo International Airport. The Russian side had no plans to meet with representatives of the US administration this week, he said. Peskov did not immediately respond to a request for further comment after news broke that Ratcliffe was aboard the plane. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. Ratcliffe’s visit to Russia was reported earlier by CBS News. The last known visit by a CIA director to Moscow was in November 2021, when William Burns, who led the agency under Joe Biden, warned Putin and his top aides not to attack Ukraine and spelled out what the consequences would be. Moscow launched its full-scale invasion within weeks. A Boeing C-17 Globemaster III at the Richmond Airshow 2025 in Australia. Photo via Getty Images Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow comes as Ukrainian long-range strikes into Russia, including the capital, have targeted energy infrastructure and online retail facilities, unnerving the population. Russia also has stepped up drone and missile strikes on Kyiv, Ukraine’s capital, and elsewhere, exploiting shortfalls of air-defence resources. President Donald Trump, at a Nato summit in Turkey in July, appeared to grant Ukraine’s long-standing request that it be able to produce US-designed Patriot air-defence missiles on its soil. He later backed away from that promise. The US aircraft that arrived in Moscow, a C-17A Globemaster III, is the Defence Department’s workhorse heavy transport plane. The airframe is especially valuable for sensitive diplomatic visits, allowing leaders to bring a tailored suite of specialised vehicles, electronic equipment and support personnel. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. The C-17A departed from Joint Base Andrews on Sunday evening, bound for Riga, Latvia, according to tracking data from Flightradar24. The plane appeared to stay in Latvia for a 24-hour layover before departing for Moscow on Tuesday morning, landing shortly after 9am local time. A second US Air Force plane, a C-40B, also took off from Joint Base Andrews and landed in Riga several hours after the C-17A’s arrival in the country. Publicly available flight tracking data does not show the C-40B on the next flight to Moscow. The aircraft is a modified business jet used to transport senior government officials. A video shared on social media Tuesday and geolocated by the Washington Post shows a motorcade of cars, some with red diplomatic plates, driving east on New Arbat Ave in central Moscow near a Russian armed forces building.
